newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sanyo, life insurers not yet agreed on loan delay.
newsitem.headline: Sanyo, life insurers not yet agreed on loan delay.

text.p: Both Sanyo Securities Co Ltd and two Japanese life insurers said on Tuesday they have not yet reached agreement on Sanyo's request for a delay in repayment of subordinated loans extended by the insurers.
"We are still negotiating," a Sanyo spokesman said. He declined to provide further details.
A Nippon Life Insurance Co spokesman said his company was still waiting for a new restructuring plan to be submitted by Sanyo Securities.
"We have said we could consider the delay if Sanyo comes up with a drastic restructuring plan, but so far we have not heard about any new plans," the spokesman said.
A spokesman for Dai-Ichi Mutual Life Insurance Co said the situation had not changed since last time Sanyo officials repeated their request last week.

Sanyo faces financial difficulties due to problem loans held at affiliated firms and protracted sluggishness in the stock market. To help bail out its group firms, the second-tier brokerage launched a nine-year restructuring programme in the 1994/95 business year.

Sanyo received subordinated loans from several major life insurance companies, including Nippon Life and Dai-Ichi Mutual Life, in an effort to increase its capital and strengthen its financial position.

The Japanese daily Sankei Shimbun said on Tuesday that life insurers are expected to comply with Sanyo's request for a delay in the repayment of subordinated loans which come due at the end of July 1998.
